requirements.text: Patients should be able to book, cancel, or reschedule appointments online.
Patients should be able to see available time slots for both GP and nurse appointments.
Patients should be able to filter their search by the type of appointment they need.
Patients should be able to flag urgent symptoms for prioritization.
Patients should receive confirmation of appointments through their preferred communication method.
GPs and nurses should be able to manage their availability easily.
Patients should log into their account to navigate to a section for repeat prescriptions.
Patients should see a list of their current medications that are eligible for repeat prescriptions.
Patients should have the option to add comments or notes with their prescription requests.
The system should notify the relevant clinician when a repeat prescription request is submitted.
Repeat prescription requests should be completed only after clinician authorization.
Patients should receive notifications when their prescription is ready.
Patients should log into their portal account and access a dedicated section for test results.
Patients should see a summary of their recent tests with status indicators for availability.
Patients should receive notifications when their test results are available for viewing.
Detailed test results along with clinician comments should be accessible in a secure area.
Any test results that require follow-up or discussion should be clearly flagged for the patient.
The portal must be cost-effective, demonstrating a clear return on investment.
The new portal must seamlessly integrate with the existing practice management system.
The portal must comply with GDPR and relevant Irish data protection legislation.
The portal should cater to patients with low digital literacy and meet accessibility standards.
Adequate training must be planned for staff to ensure proficiency in using the new system.
The portal needs to maintain high availability, ideally 99.9%, to avoid patient frustration.
